record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let E2 be the set of integers n with 1 <= n <= 20000 for which 2^9 * p is a proper divisor of n for some p in {3, 5, 7}. For the 18 orders in E2, can the finite groups of order n be enumerated up to isomorphism despite the large number of groups already occurring at each base order 2^9 * p?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let
$$E_2 = \{\, n \in \mathbb{Z} : 1 \le n \le 20000 \text{ and there exists } p \in \{3,5,7\} \text{ such that } 2^{9}\cdot p \text{ is a proper divisor of } n \,\},$$
where "proper divisor" means a divisor strictly smaller than $n$. The set $E_2$ consists of exactly $18$ integers. For each base order $b \in \{2^{9}\cdot 3,\; 2^{9}\cdot 5,\; 2^{9}\cdot 7\} = \{1536, 2560, 3584\}$, the number of pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups of order $b$ is already extremely large (in particular, this number is so large at $b = 1536$ that a complete list of the isomorphism types of groups of order $1536$ is not currently available).

Problem: For each of the $18$ orders $n \in E_2$, determine, up to isomorphism, all finite groups of order $n$. More precisely, develop a constructive classification (or a complete enumeration up to isomorphism) of the finite groups of every order $n$ in $E_2$, or else establish a definite obstruction to producing such a classification.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on the classification of finite groups of small order (including a 2024 article in Foundations of Computational Mathematics) and the GAP SmallGroups library documentation indicate that orders divisible by 2^9·3 = 1536 remain outside the range of complete enumeration: groups of order 1536 have not been fully classified, and proper multiples up to 20000 (the set E2) are likewise not enumerated. No source found announces a completion of these cases, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Finite Groups: Recent Developments and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of computational determination and enumeration of groups of small order, listing remaining open ranges.
status_evidence.claim: Groups of orders containing high 2-power factors such as 2^9·p remain unenumerated.

status_evidence.title: SmallGrp - The GAP Small Groups Library
status_evidence.snippet: The library contains groups of order at most 2000 except 1024, and certain other restricted orders; orders such as 1536 and its proper multiples up to 20000 are not included.
status_evidence.claim: The SmallGroups library does not contain groups of order 1536 or its proper multiples in E2.

status_evidence.title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies E2 as 18 orders up to 20000 for which enumeration is open.
status_evidence.claim: Enumeration for the 18 orders in E2 is posed as an open problem.
